title: Moving bank relay
summary: A low-friction puck is already sliding toward the right arm at the start, through the first of two gaps in a row of posts across the table. The right Panda's paddle must strike it. The puck must then come back through that same gap and hit the left Panda's paddle, which acts as a rebound board. The right paddle strikes the puck a second time. The puck must then come back through the second gap and hit the left board again, with the board at a clearly different position and angle from the first rebound. Finally the puck must cross a goal line in front of a backstop wall on the right arm's side, without the right paddle touching it as it crosses.
robot_setup: panda-0 (left): base at (-0.55, -0.22, 0), yaw 0 (facing +x). panda-1 (right): base at (0.74, 0.22, 0), yaw pi (facing -x). Each carries a flat rigid paddle, 0.10 m long (2 x `tool_half`, `tool_half` = 0.05 m for both arms), 0.05 m tall and 12 mm thick, on a rigid adapter on its back (tool -x) side. The tool frame is the paddle centre, with x normal to its faces, y along its length and z up. The TCP sits 0.12 m behind the paddle centre (tool -x) and 0.04 m above it. Left paddle (the rebound board) start: centre (-0.015, 0.08, 0.045), orientation identity (faces normal to world x, length along world y). Right paddle start: centre (0.27, -0.11, 0.045), quaternion (0, 0, 0, 1) (yawed 180 deg). At the start height each paddle's lower edge is 0.020 m above the table. Role labels (panda-0 / panda-1) by phase: right_first_strike preparing_board / striker; left_first_rebound rebound_operator / preparing_receiver; right_recovery_strike changing_board / striker; left_changed_rebound rebound_operator / cleared_striker; terminal_goal board_support / cleared_striker.
scene: A small orange square puck (44 mm x 44 mm, 24 mm tall) slides on the table with very little friction. At t = 0 it is already moving toward the right arm. Four short orange posts (24 mm x 50 mm, 60 mm tall) stand in a row across the table between the arms. The middle two overlap into a single block, so the row leaves two equal gaps, and the puck starts in line with the first gap. The posts are not bouncy. A long, very bouncy rail (70 mm tall) runs along the +y side of the course. A short backstop wall (0.14 m wide, 70 mm tall, not bouncy) stands behind the goal line on the right arm's side. All of these are fixed, and only the puck moves by itself. The table top is the world's z = 0 plane.
scene_privileged: Puck: box 0.044 x 0.044 x 0.024 m, mass `object_mass` = 0.035 kg, friction 0.012, restitution 0.65. At reset it is placed at (0.12, u, 0.0125), with u drawn uniformly in [-0.03, 0.01] m. Its initial velocity is (+`incoming_speed`, 0, 0) = (0.35, 0, 0) m/s, heading +x through gap 0. Table friction `table_friction` = 0.015. Route posts route_0_-1, route_0_1, route_1_-1 and route_1_1 are static (friction 0.3, restitution 0.05). Each is 0.024 (x) x 0.050 (y) x 0.060 m, centred at x = 0.16 and z = 0.03. Gap 0 is formed by the posts at y = -0.085 and 0.065: y in [-0.06, 0.04], centre -0.01. Gap 1 is formed by the posts at y = 0.085 and 0.235: y in [0.11, 0.21], centre 0.16. The posts at 0.065 and 0.085 overlap. return_rail (static, restitution 0.7): 0.48 x 0.016 x 0.070 m, centred at (0.15, 0.29, 0.035), running along x from -0.09 to 0.39. backstop (static, restitution 0.05): 0.02 x 0.14 x 0.07 m, centred at (0.48, 0.16, 0.035). Paddles: `tool_half` = 0.05, `tool_mass` = 0.2 kg, `tool_friction` = 0.3, restitution 0.05. The left arm's setup lists 0.075 m and 0.22 kg, but these are overridden by `tool_half` and `tool_mass`. The table top spans x in [-0.54, 0.70] and y in [-0.48, 0.48]. A puck sliding off it falls below z = -0.2 (generic out_of_bounds). Horizon `horizon` = 25 s. The only random draw is u, made at reset.

phases.name: right_first_strike
phases.text: The puck touches the right paddle. Any contact counts; there is no speed condition.

phases.name: left_first_rebound
phases.text: During this phase the puck's centre crosses the line x = 0.16 moving in -x, with |y - (-0.01)| < 0.048 m, i.e. back through gap 0. Moving in -x means x was >= 0.16 on the previous physics step and is < 0.16 now. After that crossing, the puck touches the left paddle. The left paddle's tool-frame pose (position and orientation) at that contact is recorded.

phases.name: right_recovery_strike
phases.text: The puck touches the right paddle more than 0.06 s after this phase began.

phases.name: left_changed_rebound
phases.text: During this phase the puck's centre crosses x = 0.16 moving in -x, with |y - 0.16| < 0.048 m, i.e. through gap 1. After that crossing, the puck touches the left paddle while two pose conditions hold. The paddle's tool-frame origin is more than 0.035 m from the recorded first-rebound position. And its orientation is rotated by more than 0.24 rad (about 13.8 deg) from the recorded orientation, i.e. |q . q_first| < cos 0.12. Contacts that do not meet the pose condition do not count, but they do not fail the task either.

phases.name: terminal_goal
phases.text: The puck's centre crosses x = 0.42 moving in +x, with |y - 0.16| < 0.055 m, while the puck is not touching the right paddle. This completes the task.

contact_rules: Each paddle may touch only the puck. The paddles must not touch the posts, the rail, the backstop, the table or the robot pedestals. No other robot part, the fingers included, may touch anything. The two arms and their paddles must never touch each other, and a paddle must not touch its own arm.
world_goals_fixed: Crossing lines for the puck's centre. Gap 0 line: x = 0.16 with |y + 0.01| < 0.048 m, crossed in -x. Gap 1 line: x = 0.16 with |y - 0.16| < 0.048 m, crossed in -x. Goal line: x = 0.42 with |y - 0.16| < 0.055 m, crossed in +x; it is announced at reset as `goal_goal` = (0.42, 0.16, 0.012).
difficulty_note: The puck barely loses speed, and each return through a post gap needs a precisely aimed hit at a narrow opening. Between its two rebounds the left board must be both moved and turned. After the second rebound the puck still has to reach the goal line.
standard_notes: The puck is already sliding toward the right arm at t = 0 and keeps sliding for a long time, so it is moving from the very first frame. Any touch by the right paddle in the first phase completes it.
